per_policy_guidance.guidance: Validated in distribution on the 12 replayed training-segment entry states: 10/12 final successes (83.3%). Invoke only in the documented regime: drawer_position > 0.26 m, red being released or settled on its outside pad, blue observed outside as the source, with source_object="blue" and destination_field="blue_goal". Its source-frame representation is intended for pickup and early carry when source displacement/rotation is the main concern, but that benefit has not been validated out of distribution. Avoid using it as the preferred confined final-alignment policy, for unreachable/collision-prone source poses, or as recovery after a suspected drop or impact. Monitor IK convergence/limit contacts, whether blue and TCP co-move after closure, red remaining on the pad, and approach to the drawer lip/wall. In both validation failures the drawer stayed open and red stayed on-pad, but blue was not inside; those runs had 73 and 65 IK-unconverged steps. IK warnings are not conclusive, however, because one successful run had 335. Replan after each eight-action chunk. Once blue appears stably carried near the drawer, hand off to destination-anchored h02; on simultaneous drawer-open/red-on-pad/blue-inside success, hand only to framework evaluation. There is no learned successor or demonstrated recovery behavior.

Strongest in-distribution evidence: 12/12 final successes (100%) from its replayed training-segment entries, with zero IK-unconverged steps in all validation runs. Prefer it for a nominal matching entry and especially once closed-finger blue/TCP co-motion suggests a stable carry and destination alignment/insertion dominates. Required destination_field is "blue_goal"; drawer_position must remain > 0.26 m, with red on or being released over its pad. It was trained over the earlier overlap as well, so it can receive control during red release, transit, approach, closure, or lift, but its principal prior is destination anchoring. Avoid treating this result as evidence for changed/rotated drawers, unreachable translated goals, wall/lip avoidance, failed-grasp recovery, or arbitrary far-displaced free sources. No validation failure was observed; runtime failure checks must therefore come from the contract: loss of blue/TCP co-motion, IK failure or limit contact, lip/wall approach, drawer at or below 0.26 m, red leaving the pad, or blue missing cavity/height bounds. Refresh the observed goal every eight-action chunk. If blue is still free and source variation dominates, hand off to h01 (particularly source rotation) or consider h04 for its source-to-goal corridor prior, while retaining the no-OOD-evidence caveat. Otherwise continue through insertion/release as needed and defer completion solely to the simultaneous task evaluator; there is no learned successor.

Validated in distribution at 10/12 final successes (83.3%). Use when entry timing within the demonstrated responsibility is uncertain but still nominal, two-frame causal history is available, and small feedback-like TCP corrections are more important than a fixed global anchor. Entry requires drawer_position > 0.26 m, red being released/settled on its pad, blue outside or held, and source_object="blue" plus destination_field="blue_goal". Avoid it for large source or destination displacement, global collision-free routing, long open-loop correction, or recovery after drops, re-grasps, or impacts; eight-step local increments can drift. Do not use the auxiliary phase class as a success or contact signal. Watch for phase/geometry disagreement, blue failing to co-move after closure, drift away from source or destination, IK/limit issues, red or drawer regressions, and lip/wall contact. In both validation failures the drawer remained open and red remained on-pad but blue was not inside; neither failure had any IK-unconverged steps, so healthy IK alone is not evidence of success. Replan every eight executed actions. Hand off to h02 when blue is stably carried toward the drawer, and to h01 for large free-source displacement; h04 is the corridor-specialized alternative for source-to-goal translation. End only on framework-observed simultaneous task success. No recovery or learned successor is established.

Validated in distribution at 11/12 final successes (91.7%). Use in the documented drawer-open/red-release-or-settled regime with source_object="blue" and destination_field="blue_goal", particularly when the source-to-destination corridor representation is an appropriate prior for acquisition and transport. The representation is designed so pickup-side targets follow the source and insertion-side targets stay goal-anchored, but robustness to translated sources or changed source-goal separation was not tested out of distribution and must not be assumed. Avoid it when source or drawer rotation is the main change, when predicted corridor progress alpha selects an implausible anchor, for unreachable/collision-prone geometry, or as drop/impact recovery. Inspect published alpha/target diagnostics: warning signs include red-release targets being dragged toward blue, pickup targets moving toward the drawer before a secure grasp, lack of blue/TCP co-motion, IK failure/limits, lip/wall approach, drawer_position <= 0.26 m, red leaving its pad, or missed final blue bounds. Its sole validation failure ended with red still on-pad but blue outside and the drawer fully closed at 0.0 after having opened; it also had 415 IK-unconverged steps and 9 gripper changes. Treat that as one observed failure pattern, not a general threshold. Refresh source and goal endpoints every eight actions. Hand off to h02 once blue is stably carried near the drawer; use h01 when source rotation dominates and h03 for small fresh-TCP corrections. Completion is only the simultaneous framework success condition; there is no learned successor.

summary:
All four policies were evaluated only from their own in-distribution training-segment entry states in the 12 demonstrations, for the fixed 1.5x budget and the same final-state rule: drawer open, red on pad, and blue inside. No out-of-distribution or recovery result exists. For a nominal matching state, h02 has the strongest evidence (12/12) and is the preferred default, especially for stable carry and final destination alignment. h04 is next (11/12) and offers a source-to-goal corridor prior, while h01 and h03 each passed 10/12 and are specialized respectively for source-frame pickup/early carry and uncertain valid timing/small incremental correction. Their coordinate constructions motivate policy choice but do not validate robustness to shifted or rotated scenes.

Across policies, require drawer_position > 0.26 m at entry, preserve red-on-pad status, refresh chunk context after every eight executed actions, and never infer grasp or success from finger closure, proximity, phase, or co-motion alone. Abort or explicitly replan rather than assuming recovery after a suspected drop, collision, wall/lip impact, sustained IK failure, or drawer/red regression. Handoff should generally move from h01/h03/h04 to h02 once blue is stably carried near the drawer. Stop only when the framework observes all three task goals simultaneously; release or high retreat is not an additional success requirement.
